name: Fossil bone
description: A long leg bone turned to brown stone, cracked in rings along the shaft.
notes: A thigh bone 400 mm long with a ball head and knob at one end and two knuckles at the other, ringed with darker cracks. clay-wet draws the stone and stone-whet the cracks. CHECK VOLUME (x6): the box counts the air round a long thin bone; the solid is close to the reference's 250 ml.

name: Plaster bone
description: A white plaster cast of a long leg bone.
notes: Same shape as the fossil bone, recoloured: chalk-white on every slot, so the cracks vanish and it reads as a smooth cast.

name: Field stone
description: A flat stone about the size of a dinner plate, the kind stacked into dry walls.
notes: A flat stone 350 by 230 mm and 35 mm thick, its edges thinning, with a darker raised patch on top. Hammering 1 because any rock this size can knock in a stake.

name: Huge fossil bone
description: A leg bone two metres long, turned to stone.
notes: The fossil bone's shape scaled to 2 m. The reference names it a replica though it is the stone one; this draft names it as the fossil. CHECK VOLUME (x5): the box counts the air round a long thin bone. The size is a placeholder for a thing too long for a pack.

name: Huge plaster bone
description: A white plaster cast of a leg bone two metres long.
notes: Same shape as the huge fossil bone, recoloured chalk-white on every slot. The reference gives the cast the stone one's weight; a real plaster cast would be lighter, kept at the reference's 70 kg. The size is a placeholder.

name: Large rock
description: A big lumpy rock with a flattish top.
notes: A rock 310 by 230 mm and 180 mm high built from three swelling lobes, a paler spur at one side. Anvil 1 follows the reference: a flat top to beat on.

name: Mineral wool batt
description: A slab of fireproof mineral wool wrapped in foil, from inside an oven or dishwasher.
notes: A batt 500 by 300 by 20 mm, foil on both faces and long sides with a taped seam, the fibre showing at both cut ends. paperboard-tan draws the fibre. The reference gives no longest side; the size fits its 3 L.

name: Canvas patch
description: A square of heavy canvas with its edges turned and stitched.
notes: A patch 150 mm square with a turned hem and a pale stitch line. CHECK VOLUME (x23): cloth is thinner than the 2 mm grain, so the box is mostly air over a thin sheet; folded in a pack it takes far less. Stack 20, since patches pile flat.
